2023_23_8_b_24680_troy_school_district_a.paragraph: Troy School District's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023, prepared by the Department of Business Services and audited by Plante & Moran, which issued an unmodified opinion dated October 3, 2023 and reported no findings or questioned costs on federal awards. Combined governmental fund balance rose $187,034,376 to $237,688,462, driven almost entirely by the first $171,370,000 series of the $555 million bond voters approved on November 8, 2022. The government-wide net position deficit narrowed by $15,751,638 to $(162,472,077), while the General Fund balance slipped $360,516 to $32,620,321, leaving unassigned reserves at 16.9 percent of 2023 operating expenditures.

**What it is**

Troy School District's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) with supplementary information for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023, presented to the Board of Education on October 17, 2023 as agenda item 8.B. Prepared by the Department of Business Services at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; transmittal letter dated October 3, 2023 signed by Deputy Superintendent Rick West and Director of Finance Kandice Moynihan. Plante & Moran issued an unmodified audit opinion dated October 3, 2023; there were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards.

**Government-wide financial position (governmental activities)**

| Item | 2023 | 2022 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Total assets | $473.1M | $275.7M |
| Deferred outflows | $131.9M | $65.1M |
| Total liabilities | $700.4M | $382.9M |
| Net pension liability | $340.4M | $210.9M |
| Net OPEB liability | $19.2M | $13.5M |
| Deferred inflows | $67.1M | $136.2M |
| Net investment in capital assets | $92.4M | $82.1M |
| Unrestricted | $(263.7)M | $(266.6)M |
| Total net position (deficit) | $(162.5)M | $(178.3)M |

Total revenue was $224.6 million against $208.8 million of expenses, producing a $15,751,638 increase in net position. Exact statement-of-activities figures: total expenses $208,835,697; charges for services $8,064,517; operating grants and contributions $60,617,779; net expense $(140,153,401); total general revenue $155,905,039; ending net position $(162,472,077).

**Fund results**

| Fund | FY2023 ending balance | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| General Fund | $32,620,321 | $(360,516) |
| 2023 Capital Projects Fund | $188,680,666 | $188,680,666 |
| Nonmajor governmental funds | $16,387,475 | $(1,285,774) |
| All governmental funds | $237,688,462 | $187,034,376 |

General Fund revenue was $189,049,577 and expenditures $189,410,093. Unassigned General Fund balance was $32,034,595, or 16.9 percent of 2023 general operating expenditures, against a board policy minimum of 15 percent. Special revenue fund balances grew from $5.9 million to $9.7 million (Food Service +$0.9 million from federal supply chain assistance, Community Service +$1.4 million, Preschool +$1.1 million from federal childcare stabilization grants). Capital project fund balances rose $182.7 million; debt service fund balances rose $0.9 million.

**Debt and capital**

Bonds outstanding grew from $116,165,000 to $271,570,000, plus unamortized premium of $25,179,339, for $296,749,339 total bonds payable. The 2023 issue was $171,370,000 at 2.75%-5.00%, maturing May 1, 2052; total remaining debt service to maturity is $433,473,045 ($271,570,000 principal, $161,903,045 interest). Standard & Poor's affirmed an AA/Stable rating in January 2023. Net capital assets were $202,522,934 (cost $414,311,763 less $211,788,829 accumulated depreciation), with $13.6 million of additions and $9,995,870 of depreciation. Construction commitments remaining totaled $32,963,954. The district collected $4.4 million of sinking fund millage.

**Pensions and outlook**

MPSERS net pension liability was $340,447,659 and net OPEB liability $19,240,985 (0.91 percent proportionate share, measured September 30, 2022, 6.00 percent discount rate). Pension contributions were $42,481,418 and OPEB contributions $7,430,175. Spring 2023 enrollment was 12,540; the 2023-24 budget assumes 12,282 pupils and a $458 foundation allowance increase to $10,332 per pupil.
2023_23_8_b_24680_troy_school_district_a.verbose:
**Identification.** Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) with supplementary information for Troy School District for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023, submitted to the Board of Education on October 17, 2023 as agenda item 8.B. Prepared by the Department of Business Services at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098-4777 (248-823-4000, fax 248-823-4013); transmittal letter dated October 3, 2023 signed by Rick West, Deputy Superintendent (rwest@troy.k12.mi.us, 248.823.4022), and Kandice Moynihan, Director of Finance. The district has no component units.

**Officials.** Board of Education: Karl Schmidt, President; Dr. Nicole Wilson, Vice President; Gary Hauff, Secretary; Trustees Vital Anne, Emina Alic, Esq., Matt Haupt, Esq., and Dr. Nancy Philippart. Administration: Richard Machesky, Ed.D., Superintendent; Rick West, Deputy Superintendent; Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent Secondary Instruction; Kristine Griffor, Assistant Superintendent Elementary Instruction; John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent Employee Services. ASBO International has awarded the district a Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for fiscal years ended June 30, 1989 through 2022; the FY2022 certificate is signed by John W. Hutchison, President, and Siobhan McMahon, CAE, Chief Operations Officer/Interim Executive Director.

**Audit.** Plante & Moran, appointed by the Troy Board of Education for 2022-23, issued an unmodified opinion on the governmental activities, each major fund, and the aggregate remaining fund information as of June 30, 2023, with a companion Government Auditing Standards report dated October 3, 2023. There were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards.

**Government-wide net position.** Net position (deficit) was $(162,472,077) at June 30, 2023 versus $(178,223,715) at June 30, 2022, a $15,751,638 improvement. Components: net investment in capital assets $92,427,309; restricted for capital projects $5,617,158, food service $3,015,211, and debt service $155,414 (restricted total $8,787,783); unrestricted $(263,687,169). Total assets were $473,162,019, including cash and cash equivalents $40,006,840, other receivables $532,785, due from other governments $29,359,729, inventory $121,941, prepaid expenses $526,658, restricted assets $200,091,132, capital assets not depreciated $5,449,400, and depreciable capital assets net $197,073,534. Deferred outflows totaled $131,860,812 (deferred charges on bond refunding $310,716; deferred pension costs $105,458,305; deferred OPEB costs $26,091,791). Total liabilities were $700,412,673, including accounts payable $5,568,084, due to other governmental units $6,727,622, accrued salaries and wages $9,974,718, accrued payroll taxes and fringe benefits $6,901,361, accrued interest payable $2,275,284, unearned revenue $3,778,838, noncurrent liabilities due within one year $21,572,288 and due in more than one year $283,925,834, net pension liability $340,447,659, and net OPEB liability $19,240,985. Deferred inflows totaled $67,082,235 (revenue in support of pension contributions made after the measurement date $24,661,370; deferred pension cost reductions $2,419,457; deferred OPEB cost reductions $40,001,408). Per the MD&A, current and other assets grew from $76.7 million to $270.6 million.

**Statement of activities.** Total expenses were $208,835,697: instruction $123,107,488; support services $69,275,079; athletics $2,361,149; food services $4,175,797; community services $4,687,389; interest $4,392,161; other debt costs $836,634. Program revenue was charges for services $8,064,517 (instruction $474,025, athletics $658,905, food services $2,390,639, community services $4,540,948) and operating grants and contributions $60,617,779 (instruction $41,012,897, support services $17,576,956, food services $2,027,926), leaving net expense of $(140,153,401). General revenue totaled $155,905,039: property taxes levied for general purposes $38,007,427, for debt service $18,910,537, and for capital projects $4,447,320; state aid not restricted to specific purposes $86,465,321; unrestricted federal grants $41,954; interest and investment earnings $4,143,480; loss on sale of capital assets $(305,026); student activities $3,370,682; other $823,344.

**Governmental funds.** Combined fund balance was $237,688,462, up $187,034,376 from $50,654,086, on assets of $277,307,921 and liabilities of $39,619,459. The General Fund held $61,484,795 of assets, $28,864,474 of liabilities, and $32,620,321 of fund balance (unassigned $32,034,595); the 2023 Capital Projects Fund $192,882,387 of assets and $188,680,666 of fund balance; nonmajor funds $22,940,739 and $16,387,475. Classifications: restricted debt service $2,430,698, capital projects $192,293,683, food service $2,952,338; committed community service $4,210,038 and student activities $2,446,386; assigned capital maintenance $672,125. Custodial funds held $95,845 of cash and $92,862 of net position after $102,535 of fundraising and contributions and $114,316 of disbursements.

**Fund revenue and expenditures.** Total governmental revenue was $235,631,022: local $77,767,307, state $129,932,089, federal $16,849,413, interdistrict $11,082,213. General Fund revenue was $189,049,577 (local $40,849,017; state $127,900,185; federal $9,219,660; interdistrict $11,080,715) against expenditures of $189,410,093, a $(360,516) change. Total expenditures were $238,943,740: instruction $127,082,439, support services $64,776,167, athletics $2,381,909, food services $4,114,838, community services $4,772,649, debt principal $15,965,000, interest $3,424,055, other debt costs $836,634, capital outlay $15,590,049. Other financing sources of $190,347,094 (debt face value $171,370,000 plus premium $18,977,094) were all in the 2023 Capital Projects Fund.

**Budget.** The final amendment was adopted in June 2023. Budgeted General Fund revenue rose $17.1 million, mainly state and federal, reflecting the 2023 State School Aid Act's categorical increases, full funding of Section 31a At-Risk revenue for hold harmless districts, and one-time Section 147c(2) revenue; federal revenue rose $1.3 million for ESSER II and Section 11t American Rescue Plan grants, and $1.2 million of transfers from special revenue funds was removed. Revenue: original $172,213,454, final $189,304,235, actual $189,049,577. Expenditures: original $176,243,584, final $189,751,106, actual $189,410,093. Actuals by function: basic programs $93,093,879; added needs $30,968,129; adult/continuing education $868,356; pupil support $14,256,909; instructional staff $11,524,085; general administration $1,732,483; school administration $10,453,879; business $1,632,735; operations and maintenance $13,909,481; pupil transportation $4,138,063; central $3,721,936; athletics $2,414,194; community services $217,564; debt service $478,400. Ending General Fund balance beat the final budget by $86,355.

**Nonmajor fund detail.** Special revenue ending balances: Food Service $3,015,211 (+$966,563), Community Service $2,326,059 (+$1,385,377), Troy Career Center Fund $0, Troy School District Preschool Fund $1,883,979 (+$1,115,576), Troy School and Student Activities Fund $2,446,386 (+$300,441). Debt service funds: 2014 Debt Fund $0 (-$180,406), 2015 Refunding Debt Fund $767,279, 2016 Debt Fund $497,827, 2019 Debt Fund $334,362, 2021 Refunding Series A Debt Fund $0, 2021 Refunding Series B Debt Fund $831,230. Capital project funds: 2019 Capital Projects Fund $1,685,663 (-$5,154,459), Capital Maintenance Fund $672,125, Sinking Fund $1,927,354 (-$859,672).

**Capital assets.** Net capital assets were $202,522,934 versus $198,957,764 in 2022. Gross cost $414,311,763: land $1,861,010; construction in progress $3,588,390; buildings and improvements $356,601,423; furniture and equipment $51,730,652; lease asset - building $530,288; accumulated depreciation and amortization $211,788,829. Additions of $13.6 million covered building renovations, site work, and technology infrastructure. Depreciation and amortization of $9,995,870 was charged to instruction $4,112,835, support services $5,668,498, community services $101,531, food services $48,017, and athletics $64,989. Construction commitments remaining were $426,928 in the 2019 Capital Projects Fund, $28,019,164 in the 2023 Capital Projects Fund, and $4,517,862 in the Sinking Fund, on $6,066,766 spent to date. Capitalization threshold $5,000; useful lives 20-50 years for buildings, 5-10 for furniture and equipment.

**Debt.** General obligation bonds outstanding rose from $116,165,000 to $271,570,000; with unamortized premium of $25,179,339, total bonds payable was $296,749,339. Outstanding issues: $31,930,000 2015 refunding bond, 5.00%, final maturity May 1, 2026, $9,675,000 outstanding; $40,000,000 2016 GO bond, 2.94%-4.50%, May 1, 2032, $30,550,000; $7,125,000 2018 GO bond, 3.00%-3.75%, May 1, 2040, $6,340,000; $22,630,000 2019 GO bond, 5.00%, May 1, 2034, $18,325,000; $6,100,000 2020 GO bond, 2.00%, May 1, 2035, $5,020,000; $33,315,000 2021 refunding bond, 0.50%-1.56%, May 1, 2028, $30,290,000; $171,370,000 2023 GO bond, 2.75%-5.00%, May 1, 2052, $171,370,000. Debt service to maturity totals $433,473,045 ($271,570,000 principal plus $161,903,045 interest), with $31,815,482 due in 2024. Other long-term liabilities: leases $333,527 (the Troy Career Center building, $359,563 of remaining payments through 2027), compensated absences $8,262,756, other termination benefits $152,500; total governmental long-term debt $305,498,122, with $21,572,288 due within one year. S&P affirmed an AA/Stable rating in January 2023. The 15 percent statutory limit equals $694.6 million; unqualified GO debt of $11.4 million is far below it, and qualified (state-backed) debt totals $260.2 million.

**Deposits and restricted assets.** Bank deposits of $47,246,346 were uninsured and uncollateralized; nine institutions are designated and three were used. Investments were $192,940,328 in the Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Cash Management Money Market Fund and $1,690,622 in MILAF MAX Class, both AAAm by S&P, totaling $194,630,950. Restricted assets of $200,091,132 comprise unspent bond proceeds and interest $194,630,950, unspent sinking fund taxes $3,059,083, and unspent debt service taxes $2,401,099. Unearned revenue of $3,778,838 comprises student lunch accounts $110,721, tuition and fees in advance $514,652, and categorical aid received before eligibility $3,153,465. Interfund balances totaled $6,668,836. The district participates in the SET-SEG shared-risk pool for property and general liability.

**MPSERS pension and OPEB.** Net pension liability was $340,447,659 and net OPEB liability $19,240,985, both measured September 30, 2022 from a September 30, 2021 valuation rolled forward; the district's proportion was 0.90524 percent for pension and 0.90842 percent for OPEB, versus about 0.89 percent in 2021. FY2023 pension contributions were $42,481,418, including $15,584,907 of state UAAL stabilization revenue and a $9,076,463 one-time Section 147c(2) state payment; OPEB contributions were $7,430,175. Pension expense recognized was $43,642,684; OPEB recovery was $6,981,694. Statutorily required contributions were $41,845,623 for pension (48.61 percent of $86,081,809 covered payroll) and $6,928,897 for OPEB (8.05 percent). Pension deferred outflows were $105,458,305 against $2,419,457 of inflows; OPEB deferred outflows $26,091,791 against $40,001,408. The discount and investment return rate was 6.00 percent, down 0.80 points for pension and 0.95 for OPEB; salary increases 2.75-11.55 percent; COLA 3.00 percent noncompounded for MIP members; mortality basis RP-2014 with MP-2017 projection. At 5.00 percent the net pension liability would be $449,264,431 and at 7.00 percent $250,777,736; net OPEB liability $32,274,902 and $8,264,810. Payables to the pension and OPEB plans were $9,208,156 and $999,310. Plan fiduciary net position was 60.77 percent of total pension liability and 83.09 percent of total OPEB liability.

**Taxes and statistics.** Tax year 2022 taxable value was $4,623,935,940 (residential $3,099,545,240; commercial $979,250,150; industrial $255,866,910; personal property $289,273,640) at 26.1344 mills, estimated actual value $9,247,871,880. Direct 2022 millage was 3.0693 homestead operating, 18.0000 non-homestead, 4.1000 debt, 0.9651 sinking fund. The FY2023 levy of $61,388,795 was 99.68 percent collected. Largest taxpayer: Somerset Collections, $60,876,330 taxable value. Largest employer: William Beaumont Hospital, 2,300 employees, with the district second at 1,331. Tax abatements under PA 198 of 1974 and brownfield agreements cut revenue $105,000, with about $90,000 reimbursed by the State. Net general bonded debt was $294,318,642, 6.37 percent of taxable value and $3,351 per capita on a population of 87,830; total direct and overlapping debt $295,151,914. FTE staff totaled 1,082 and teaching staff 855; average teacher salary $77,080; cost per pupil $15,104; 16.00 percent qualified for free or reduced meals. Enrollment of 12,540 spanned 12 elementary buildings (5,071), 4 middle schools (2,835), 4 high schools (4,426), and early childhood (208), on 448.74 acres and 2,185,181 square feet plus 128.30 acres of vacant property, served by 74 buses. Voters approved the $555 million bond on November 8, 2022, to be issued in three series over six years with projects planned over 10 to 12 years; the 2023-24 budget adopted in June 2023 assumes 12,282 pupils and a $458 foundation allowance increase to $10,332 per pupil, with about 65.5 percent of General Fund revenue from the foundation allowance and state sources, and management warns that after 2023-24, as ESSER funding ends, difficult decisions will be needed to keep the budget balanced.
